simple.meaning: צִי (tsîy) is a Hebrew word meaning “a ship (as a fixture ).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: צִי (H6716) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Numbers 24:24, with occurrences in Numbers, Isaiah, Ezekiel, Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to צִי (H6716) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in צִי (H6716) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: צִי (tsîy) / H6716 is traced through Numbers 24:24, Isaiah 33:21, Ezekiel 30:9, Daniel 11:30 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H6716. tsiy I. צִי noun masculine Isa 33:21 ship (loan-word from Egyptian t'a£ , according to Bondi 66 , compare Erman ZMG xivi (1892),123 DHM VOJ viii. 7, 165 ); — absolute אַדִּיר צִי 33:21 a majestic ship ; plural צִים Num 24:24 (JE), Ezek 30:9 ( ׳בַּצּ ; but ᵐ5 σπεύδοντες , compare ᵑ6 , whence Co Berthol אָצִים ). צִים צִיּים, see I, II. ׳צִ . צִין proper name, of a location see צִן צִינֹק see צנק . צִיעֹר see צער . ציף see II. צוּף . I. צִיצָה צִיץ v, I.[[ צוּץ ].

occurrences.englishText: But ships shall come from the coast of Kittim.
But there Yahweh will be with us in majesty,
“ ‘ “In that day messengers will go out from before me in ships to make the careless Ethiopians afraid. There will be anguish on them, as in the day of Egypt; for, behold, it comes.”

For ships of Kittim will come against him. Therefore he will be grieved, and will return, and have indignation against the holy covenant, and will take action. He will even return, and have regard to those who forsake the holy covenant.
